name: README.md
html:
media — decoded image/video textured quad

~46 KB. Lazy artifact — mounts when a GPU-paintable media surface appears. The <img>/<video> DOM stays the semantic + fallback layer.

 mountWebGpuWidget(MEDIA, canvas)
        │
        ▼
 Media::init → one rgba texture + sampler + unit-quad pipeline
        │
        ▼
 uploads:
   upload_bitmap(ImageBitmap)  — still image, hardware-decoded
   push_frame(VideoFrame)      — WebCodecs frame, same copy path
        │
        ▼
 per frame: cover-fit textured quad (uv_rect crops letterbox)

Why no image crate

The browser decodes JPEG/PNG/WebP off-main-thread already — a Rust decoder would add ~800 KB AND run slower. JS hands us an ImageBitmap (still) or VideoFrame (WebCodecs) and copyExternalImageToTexture moves pixels GPU→GPU — no CPU readback ever.

  • upload_bitmap(bmp) — still frames; rebinds the texture.
  • push_frame(vf) — video frames via requestVideoFrameCallback (NOT per rAF — decoder-driven).
  • set_uv_rect(x,y,w,h) — cover-fit crop in uv space, JS-computed.
